name: Game UI
summary: Readable over motion, reachable mid-play and generous with feedback: HUD at the edges, big buttons, clear reward moments.
principles: The play area is the focal point; UI hugs the edges and never covers the action.
Everything must read at a glance over busy, moving backgrounds.
Every input gets immediate feedback (visual, audio and haptic where available) within 100ms.
Rewards are moments: make them big, brief and skippable.
Playful does not mean noisy: one accent, consistent outline weight, a limited palette.
structure_note: Layered: game canvas, HUD layer at the screen edges (score and resources top, actions bottom), modal layer for pause, results and rewards.

sections.name: HUD
sections.purpose: Show the state the player needs mid-play: score, lives, time, currency.
guidance: Top-left and top-right corners for status; keep the center clear.
Numbers use a chunky display font with tabular figures so they do not jitter as they change.
Group related values in one pill or plate with a solid background, not floating text.

sections.name: Controls
guidance: Primary action buttons at least 64dp (or px), bottom corners in the thumb arcs.
Pause always available in a corner, at least 48dp, never next to the primary action.
Clear pressed states (scale to 0.96 and darken), no hover-only affordances on touch.

sections.name: Readability over backgrounds
sections.purpose: Keep text legible over any scene.
guidance: Put text on solid plates or use a 2-3dp outline or stroke in a dark ink color; never rely on drop shadows alone.
Minimum 16 for in-game text, 20+ for anything read mid-action.
Check contrast against the brightest and darkest parts of the scene.

sections.name: Menus
guidance: One big primary button (Play) per screen; everything else secondary.
Level select as a clear grid or path with locked, current and completed states.
Settings include sound, music, haptics, reduced motion and colorblind-safe options.

sections.name: Reward and feedback moments
sections.purpose: Make progress feel good without slowing play.
guidance: Score pops, combo counters and star reveals take 300-800ms and can be tapped to skip.
Use scale and opacity; avoid full-screen flashes (photosensitivity) and long blocking animations.
Failure is encouraging and fast: one tap to retry.

sections.name: Results screen
sections.purpose: Summarize the run and offer the next step.
guidance: The outcome (stars, score) is the focal point; best score below in a smaller role.
Primary: Next level or Retry. Secondary: Home, Share.

states.name: Paused
states.guidance: Dim the scene with a solid scrim (not blur), show Resume as the primary action.

states.name: Loading
states.guidance: Short tips or a progress bar with real progress; never a spinner over a frozen frame.

states.name: Offline or no ads
states.guidance: Rewards and progress never depend on a network call the player cannot see.

states.name: Locked
states.guidance: Locked content shows what unlocks it, with the requirement in plain words.

accessibility: Never use color alone for game state (add shapes, icons or patterns); offer colorblind-safe palettes.
Respect reduced motion: replace screen shake and flashes with simple fades.
Remappable or large controls; avoid time-critical precision taps for basic progress.
Subtitles or captions for dialogue and important audio cues.
avoid: Neon glows and lens flares on every element
Emoji standing in for game icons
